newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: OLYMPICS-SYDNEY ORGANISERS SET UP OLYMPIC 2000 TRANSPORT BODY.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-SYDNEY ORGANISERS SET UP OLYMPIC 2000 TRANSPORT BODY.

text.p: Sydney 2000 Olympics organisers announced on Tuesday that a central body would co-ordinate transport needs to avoid the problems that plagued the Atlanta Games.
Olympics Minister Michael Knight said the newly-created Olympics Roads and Transport Authority would manage road, rail and ferry services during the Games.
The authority would ensure athletes, officials and spectators reached events on time, and that the transport system operated smoothly for other users.
"A successful Games is not just great sport and great venues in a great city. The transport plan is part of the success," said New South Wales state premier Bob Carr.

Carr said the need for a single Olympics roads and transport organisation was one of the key lessons from Atlanta, which suffered from traffic congestion and a bus system for athletes, specatators and media that did not meet demand.
Olympic inspectors in 1996 listed transport as a mjaor challenge for Sydney, which plans to use rail and buses to take most spectators to the main venue in the city's west.
Knight has also announced some 6,000 international media representatives will be housed in a former hospital, four kms (2.5 miles) from the central Games venue of Homebush Bay.
Organisers expect about 15,000 local and international media to attend the Olympics, including technical and ancillary staff.
Knight said the lack of a centralised media base in Atlanta added to transport and communications problems.
